2.original: Mon lean okta sápmelaš, guhte lean bargan visot sámi bargguid ja mon dovddan visot sámi dili.
2.translation: I am a Sámi who has done all sorts of Sámi work and I know all about Sámi conditions.
2.original_formatted: Mon lean okta sápmelaš , guhte lean bargan visot sámi bargguid ja mon dovddan visot sámi dili .
2.translation_formatted: I am a Sámi who has done all sorts of Sámi work and I know all about Sámi conditions .

3.original: Ja mon lean ipmirdan, ahte Ruoŧa hállehus háliida min veahkehit nu olu go sáhttá, muhto sii eai oaččo riekta čielgasa, jur got dat lea min eallin ja dilli, deinnago sápmelaš ii sáhte jur juste čilget nu got lea.
3.translation: I have come to understand that the Swedish government wants to help us as much as it can, but they don't get things right regarding our lives and conditions, because no Sámi can explain to them exactly how things are.
3.original_formatted: Ja mon lean ipmirdan , ahte Ruoŧa hállehus háliida min veahkehit nu olu go sáhttá , muhto sii eai oaččo riekta čielgasa , jur got dat lea min eallin ja dilli , deinnago sápmelaš ii sáhte jur juste čilget nu got lea .
3.translation_formatted: I have come to understand that the Swedish government wants to help us as much as it can , but they don't get things right regarding our lives and conditions , because no Sámi can explain to them exactly how things are .

4.original: Ja dasa lea dát sivva: go sápmelaš boahtá moskkus gámmirii, de son ii ipmir ii báljo maidege, go ii biegga beasa bossut njuni vuostá.
4.translation: And this is the reason: when a Sámi becomes closed up in a room, then he does not understand much of anything, because he cannot put his nose to the wind.
4.original_formatted: Ja dasa lea dát sivva : go sápmelaš boahtá moskkus gámmirii , de son ii ipmir ii báljo maidege , go ii biegga beasa bossut njuni vuostá .
4.translation_formatted: And this is the reason : when a Sámi becomes closed up in a room , then he does not understand much of anything , because he cannot put his nose to the wind .

5.original: Su jurdagat eai golgga, go leat seainnit ja moskkus oaivvi nalde.
5.translation: His thoughts don't flow because there are walls and his mind is closed in.
5.original_formatted: Su jurdagat eai golgga , go leat seainnit ja moskkus oaivvi nalde .
5.translation_formatted: His thoughts don't flow because there are walls and his mind is closed in .

9.original: Mon lean jurddašan, ahte dat livččui buoremus, jos livččui dakkár girji, masa lea visot čállojuvvon bajás sámi eallin ja dilli, vai ii dárbbaš jearrat, got lea sámi dilli, ja vai eai beasa botnjat nuppe_ládje, dakkárat guđet háliidit sámiid nala gielistit, ja botnjat viso beare sámiid sivalažžan, go leat riiddut dálolaččaid ja sámiid gaskkas Norggas ja Ruoŧas.
9.translation: I have been thinking that it would be best if there were a book in which everything was written about Sámi life and conditions, so that people wouldn't have to ask how Sámi conditions are, and so that people wouldn't misconstrue things, particularly those who want to lie about the Sámi and claim that only the Sámi are at fault when disputes arise between settlers and Sámi in Norway and Sweden.
9.original_formatted: Mon lean jurddašan , ahte dat livččui buoremus , jos livččui dakkár girji , masa lea visot čállojuvvon bajás sámi eallin ja dilli , vai ii dárbbaš jearrat , got lea sámi dilli , ja vai eai beasa botnjat nuppe_ládje , dakkárat guđet háliidit sámiid nala gielistit , ja botnjat viso beare sámiid sivalažžan , go leat riiddut dálolaččaid ja sámiid gaskkas Norggas ja Ruoŧas .
9.translation_formatted: I have been thinking that it would be best if there were a book in which everything was written about Sámi life and conditions , so that people wouldn’t have to ask how Sámi conditions are , and so that people wouldn’t misconstrue things , particularly those who want to lie about the Sámi and claim that only the Sámi are at fault when disputes arise between settlers and Sámi in Norway and Sweden .

13.original: Boarráseamos muitalusat sámiid birra, dat maid nubbi sápmi lea muitalan nuppi sápmái.
13.translation: The Oldest Stories of the Sámi Such As Told From One Sámi To Another.
13.original_formatted: Boarráseamos muitalusat sámiid birra , dat maid nubbi sápmi lea muitalan nuppi sápmái .
13.translation_formatted: The Oldest Stories of the Sámi Such As Told From One Sámi To Another

14.original: Dás leat juohkelágáš muitalusat , muhto ii leat vissis leatgo jur njuolga , go eai leat čállojuvvon .
14.translation: Herein are all sorts of stories , but it is not certain whether they are true , since they haven't been written down before .
14.original_formatted: Dás leat juohkelágáš muitalusat , muhto ii leat vissis leatgo jur njuolga , go eai leat čállojuvvon .
14.translation_formatted: Herein are all sorts of stories , but it is not certain whether they are true , since they haven't been written down before .

15.original: Muitalus sápmelaččaid birra, gos sii leat vuohččan orron, ja got sin dilli lea leamaš, ja mainna sii leat eallán ja gos sii leat boahtán.
15.translation: A Story About The Sámi, Where They Used To Live, And How Their Conditions Were There, And How They Lived, And Where They Came From One never hears about the Sámi's arrival, as if they had come from somewhere else.
15.original_formatted: Muitalus sápmelaččaid birra , gos sii leat vuohččan orron , ja got sin dilli lea leamaš , ja mainna sii leat eallán ja gos sii leat boahtán .
15.translation_formatted: A Story About The Sámi , Where They Used To Live , And How Their Conditions Were There , And How They Lived , And Where They Came From One never hears about the Sámi's arrival , as if they had come from somewhere else .

68.translation: A Story Of What Happened When The Number Of People Increased And Began Seeking Land.
68.orginal: Muitalus das, got lea Sámis geavvan, go olbmot lassánedje ja álge ohcat eatnamiid.
68.translation_formatted: A Story Of What Happened When The Number Of People Increased And Began Seeking Land They came by way of the sea to the northwest outcropping and frightened the Sámi away from the coastal areas .
68.original_formatted: Muitalus das , got lea Sámis geavvan , go olbmot lassánedje ja álge ohcat eatnamiid .

80.original: Okta lea dáhpáhus, go bođii dárrolaš Njuorjovuopmegierragii gos ledje sámit orrume.
80.translation: It once happened that a Norwegian settler came to the place where the Sámi were living at the Njuorjovuopme uplands.
80.original_formatted: Okta lea dáhpáhus , go bođii dárrolaš Njuorjovuopmegierragii gos ledje sámit orrume .
80.translation_formatted: It once happened that a Norwegian settler came to the place where the Sámi were living at the Njuorjovuopme uplands .

83.original: Ja dan dáža namma leai Jubonaš.
83.translation: And that Norwegian's name was Jubonash.
83.original_formatted: Ja dan dáža namma leai Jubonaš .
83.translation_formatted: And that Norwegian's name was Jubonash .

87.original: Ja son viegai dohko ja časkkii dan sámi jámas.
87.translation: And he rushed up there and struck that Sámi dead.
87.original_formatted: Ja son viegai dohko ja časkkii dan sámi jámas .
87.translation_formatted: And he rushed up there and struck that Sámi dead .

91.original: Ja son dovddai, ahte dat lea stuorimus elolaš, ja namma lea dan sámis Huika.
91.translation: And he knew that this had been the man with a big herd and the name of this Sámi was Huika.
91.original_formatted: Ja son dovddai , ahte dat lea stuorimus elolaš , ja namma lea dan sámis Huika .
91.translation_formatted: And he knew that this had been the man with a big herd and the name of this Sámi was Huika .

99.original: Ja gal velá leat dážat goddán ovtta sámi, Gárasavvona vuloš sámi.
99.translation: And the Norwegians killed another Sámi, a man from Gárasavvon.
99.original_formatted: Ja gal velá leat dážat goddán ovtta sámi , Gárasavvona vuloš sámi .
99.translation_formatted: And the Norwegians killed another Sámi , a man from Gárasavvon .

125.original: Riidin gohččojuvvo dat, mii lea allat ja olu rássi.
125.translation: Riidi is what one calls a summit which is high and has lots of grass.
125.original_formatted: Riidin gohččojuvvo dat , mii lea allat ja olu rássi .
125.translation_formatted: Riidi is what one calls a summit which is high and has lots of grass .

126.original: Báhkkan boazu ruohttá bajás gáissáide, dakkár báktegaskkaide, gos ii beasa bajás iige vulos, jos ii muitte jur dakko boahtit gokko lea mannan.
126.translation: In the heat, a reindeer will rush up toward the snowy peaks and into box canyons where they can pass neither in nor out unless they remember to come out exactly as they went in.
126.original_formatted: Báhkkan boazu ruohttá bajás gáissáide , dakkár báktegaskkaide , gos ii beasa bajás iige vulos , jos ii muitte jur dakko boahtit gokko lea mannan .
126.translation_formatted: In the heat , a reindeer will rush up toward the snowy peaks and into box canyons where they can pass neither in nor out unless they remember to come out exactly as they went in .

276.original: Go lea čoaskkis, de galbmo gietkka dan_botta_go mánná bassojuvvo, ja de adnojuvvo báhkka geađgi gietkama siste vai bissu liekkasin.
276.translation: When it is cold out, the gietkka gets cold while the baby is out being washed and so a hot stone is placed inside the gietkka so that it remains warm
276.original_formatted: Go lea čoaskkis , de galbmo gietkka dan_botta_go mánná bassojuvvo , ja de adnojuvvo báhkka geađgi gietkama siste vai bissu liekkasin .
276.translation_formatted: When it is cold out , the gietkka gets cold while the baby is out being washed and so a hot stone is placed inside the gietkka so that it remains warm .

277.original: Ja dat geavvan lea máŋgga geardde nu, ahte ii muitte eadni váldit geađggi eret gietkama siste ja de šaddá mánná biddjojuvvot báhkka geađggi nala, ja de gal buollá čielgi.
277.translation: And it has happened many a time that a mother doesn't remember to take the stone out of the gietkka, and the baby is placed back inside on top of the stone and that burns its back.
277.original_formatted: Ja dat geavvan lea máŋgga geardde nu , ahte ii muitte eadni váldit geađggi eret gietkama siste ja de šaddá mánná biddjojuvvot báhkka geađggi nala , ja de gal buollá čielgi .
277.translation_formatted: And it has happened many a time that a mother doesn't remember to take the stone out of the gietkka , and the baby is placed back inside on top of the stone and that burns its back .

278.original: Mánná bárgu, muhto ii eadni dieđe, mii lea mánás go bárgu, muhto ferte goitge nuollat.
278.translation: The baby cries but the mother doesn't know why, but she has to take it out again .
278.original_formatted: Mánná bárgu , muhto ii eadni dieđe , mii lea mánás go bárgu , muhto ferte goitge nuollat .
278.translation_formatted: The baby cries but the mother doesn't know why , but she has to take it out again .

279.original: Ja de easka oaidná got mánás lea geavvan, ja de eadni rávki dál šaddá moraštit ja čierrut nu garrasit ahte goase jierbmi seahkana.
279.translation: And it is only then that she sees what has happened, and then the poor mother is distraught and cries so hard that she nearly loses her mind.
279.original_formatted: Ja de easka oaidná got mánás lea geavvan , ja de eadni rávki dál šaddá moraštit ja čierrut nu garrasit ahte goase jierbmi seahkana .
279.translation_formatted: And it is only then that she sees what has happened , and then the poor mother is distraught and cries so hard that she nearly loses her mind .

280.original: Ja das šaddá mánnái garra gihpu, ja go dal viimmat buorrána, de ii goitge šatta jur dearvvaš olmmoš.
280.translation: And from this the baby suffers terrible pain and when it finally heals, it won't be a very healthy person.
280.original_formatted: Ja das šaddá mánnái garra gihpu , ja go dal viimmat buorrána , de ii goitge šatta jur dearvvaš olmmoš .
280.translation_formatted: And from this the baby suffers terrible pain and when it finally heals , it won't be a very healthy person .

281.translation: Sometimes it will develop a crooked back.
281.translation_formatted: Sometimes it will develop a crooked back .

940.original: Ja goađit dat adnojit maiddá duoddariin dakkár báikkiin, gos ii leat muorra dan meari ahte boalddálii ja livččui suodji.
940.translation: They also have goađit up in the mountains in places where there isn't enough wood to use as firewood or to provide shelter.
940.original_formatted: Ja goađit dat adnojit maiddá duoddariin dakkár báikkiin , gos ii leat muorra dan meari ahte boalddálii ja livččui suodji .
940.translation_formatted: They also have goađit up in the mountains in places where there isn't enough wood to use as firewood or to provide shelter .

941.original: Ja boaldinmuorat geasehuvvojit guhkkin beanagullamiid duohkennai.
941.translation: So they must bring their firewood from afar, from many a beanagullan away.
941.original_formatted: Ja boaldinmuorat geasehuvvojit guhkkin beanagullamiid duohkennai .
941.translation_formatted: So they must bring their firewood from afar , from many a beanagullan away .

942.original: Ja go lea garra dálki, de ii leat maiddá hávski, go biegga lea nu garas ahte ii biso goahti iežá ládje go čadnojuvvo birra juohke guovllus, ja gierresiid geasašit birra goađi ja deaddalit, vai ii biegga oaččo gaikkodit.
942.translation: And when it is hard weather it is not pleasant, as the wind is so harsh that one cannot keep the goahti upright by staking it out all around and placing the sleds up against the sides of the goahti so that the wind can't blow it open.
942.original_formatted: Ja go lea garra dálki , de ii leat maiddá hávski , go biegga lea nu garas ahte ii biso goahti iežá ládje go čadnojuvvo birra juohke guovllus , ja gierresiid geasašit birra goađi ja deaddalit , vai ii biegga oaččo gaikkodit .
942.translation_formatted: And when it is hard weather it is not pleasant , as the wind is so harsh that one cannot keep the goahti upright by staking it out all around and placing the sleds up against the sides of the goahti so that the wind can't blow it open .

996.original: Čilgehus dasa manin galgá okta siida atnit guovtti sajis bohccuid.
996.translation: An Explanation of Why it is Necessary for a Siida to Divide the Reindeer into Two Parts.
996.original_formatted: Čilgehus dasa manin galgá okta siida atnit guovtti sajis bohccuid .
996.translation_formatted: An Explanation of Why it is Necessary for a Siida to Divide the Reindeer into Two Parts .

997.original: Dat lea danin_go luovvasat leat nu hilbadat, ahte sin galgá višahit nu garrasit, dan sivas go luovvasat mannet beare njolggi ja čuoskku juohke guvlui, go lea velá čoaskkis ja unnán biebmu, headju jeagil ja bievllat unnán.
997.translation: The reason for this is that the male reindeer are so unruly that they must be managed harshly:  they trot and gallop all over the place when it is still cold out and there is little food,  poor lichen growth and little open ground.
997.original_formatted: Dat lea danin_go luovvasat leat nu hilbadat , ahte sin galgá višahit nu garrasit , dan sivas go luovvasat mannet beare njolggi ja čuoskku juohke guvlui , go lea velá čoaskkis ja unnán biebmu , headju jeagil ja bievllat unnán .
997.translation_formatted: The reason for this is that the male reindeer are so unruly that they must be managed harshly :  they trot and gallop all over the place when it is still cold out and there is little food ,  poor lichen growth and little open ground .

998.original: Ja áldoeallu lea váralaš: dan galggalii sáhttit nu siivvut reainnidit go lea máŧolaš.
998.translation: And it is a dangerous time for the cow herd:  they must be herded as carefully as possible.
998.original_formatted: Ja áldoeallu lea váralaš ; dan galggalii sáhttit nu siivvut reainnidit go lea máŧolaš .
998.translation_formatted: And it is a dangerous time for the cow herd :  they must be herded as carefully as possible .

999.original: Jos áldduid šaddá višahit garrasit, de šaddet hilbadat, ja nubbi dat, ahte go áldduid šaddá višahit sakka, de reitojit, ja lea bahá beatnagat borret misiid.
999.translation: If the cow herd is managed harshly it will become unruly, and also, if the cows are driven in this way, they will go into labor early and the dogs are bad for eating the calves.
999.original_formatted: Jos áldduid šaddá višahit garrasit , de šaddet hilbadat , ja nubbi dat , ahte go áldduid šaddá višahit sakka , de reitojit , ja lea bahá beatnagat borret misiid .
999.translation_formatted: If the cow herd is managed harshly it will become unruly ,  and also ,  if the cows are driven in this way ,  they will go into labor early and the dogs are bad for eating the calves .

1000.original: Ja dat álddut, mat leat easka miesi njoallume, de dat ballájit eret miesi nalde, go beana oaguha garrasit dohko bohccuid.
1000.translation: And those cows that have not yet calved,  and who are just giving birth,  these will be frightened away from their calves when a dog comes chasing the reindeer hard.
1000.original_formatted: Ja dat álddut , mat leat easka miesi njoallume , de dat ballájit eret miesi nalde , go beana oaguha garrasit dohko bohccuid .
1000.translation_formatted: And those cows that have not yet calved ,  and who are just giving birth ,  these will be frightened away from their calves when a dog comes chasing the reindeer hard .

3041.original: Ja soai leigga goappašat nu duihmmit, ahte eaba ipmirdan das maidege got áigi manná, goas áhkká máná oaččui .
3041.translation: And both of them were so dimwitted that they didn't know how much time passes before a woman gives birth.
3041.original_formatted: Ja soai leigga goappašat nu duihmmit , ahte eaba ipmirdan das maidege got áigi manná , goas áhkká máná oaččui .
3041.translation_formatted: And both of them were so dimwitted that they didn't know how much time passes before a woman gives birth .

3042.original: Muhto de Ándaras-gállá nuorat nieida vuolgá geahččat oappás.
3042.translation: But then old Ándaras's younger daughter came to visit her sister.
3042.original_formatted: Muhto de Ándaras-gállá nuorat nieida vuolgá geahččat oappás .
3042.translation_formatted: But then old Ándaras's younger daughter came to visit her sister .

3043.original: Ja de son bođii, ja de Márjá leai juo nu, ahte ii dovdan oappásge, son lea nu skibas.
3043.translation: And when she got there, Márjá was so ill that she couldn't even recognize her own sister.
3043.original_formatted: Ja de son bođii , ja de Márjá leai juo nu , ahte ii dovdan oappásge , son lea nu skibas .
3043.translation_formatted: And when she got there , Márjá was so ill that she couldn't even recognize her own sister .

3044.original: Ja de son vulggii viežžat lasi olbmuid .
3044.translation: And so she set off at once to bring more people .
3044.original_formatted: Ja de son vulggii viežžat lasi olbmuid .
3044.translation_formatted: And so she set off at once to bring more people .

3045.original: Muhto Márjá leai skibas golbma mánu.
3045.translation: And Márjá remained ill for three months after that.
3045.original_formatted: Muhto Márjá leai skibas golbma mánu .
3045.translation_formatted: And Márjá remained ill for three months after that .

3046.translation: And the wolves killed forty head of reindeer.
3046.translation_formatted: And the wolves killed forty head of reindeer .

3047.original: Ja nelgo eallu nu_ahte váibe bohccot.
3047.translation: And the herd became so hungry that the reindeer became exhausted.
3047.original_formatted: Ja nelgo eallu nu_ahte váibe bohccot .
3047.translation_formatted: And the herd became so hungry that the reindeer became exhausted .

3048.original: Ja das lea váruhus, ahte eai galgga okto siidii mannat go eai leat liigeolbmot, ja áhkká lea gassadin.
3048.translation: And this may serve as a warning not to be in a siida all by oneself when one's wife is expecting.
3048.original_formatted: Ja das lea váruhus , ahte eai galgga okto siidii mannat go eai leat liigeolbmot , ja áhkká lea gassadin .
3048.translation_formatted: And this may serve as a warning not to be in a siida all by oneself when one's wife is expecting .

3049.original: Vaikko ii son šaddan velge geafi, muhto su áhkká šattai dan rájes skihpalaš, son šattai lihkadit, ovdal_go leai dearvvasnuvvan.
3049.translation: Although he did not become poor as a result of this all, still his wife became sickly thereafter; she had had to get back on her feet before she was fully recovered.
3049.original_formatted: Vaikko ii son šaddan velge geafi , muhto su áhkká šattai dan rájes skihpalaš , son šattai lihkadit , ovdal_go leai dearvvasnuvvan .
3049.translation_formatted: Although he did not become poor as a result of this all , still his wife became sickly thereafter ; she had had to get back on her feet before she was fully recovered .

3050.original: Ja son šattai galbmot maiddá, ja son oaččui čoaskinvigi dan rájes iige šat lean nu dearvvaš go ovdal.
3050.translation: And she had gotten chilled, so that she suffered from chills ever after and was never quite the same again.
3050.original_formatted: Ja son šattai galbmot maiddá , ja son oaččui čoaskinvigi dan rájes iige šat lean nu dearvvaš go ovdal .
3050.translation_formatted: And she had gotten chilled , so that she suffered from chills ever after and was never quite the same again .

3052.original: Stuora gávvila, nana nana nana voja voja nana nana nana, ii oktage diehtán, leago guolli dahe loddi, voja voja voja nana nana nana, stuora gávvila, voja voja nana, mieđábealde stuora bielluin guđodii, voja voja nana nana, bárdnelunttaid dorvu, go heahti bođii, go gávnnahalle suolabarggus, voja voja nana nana.
3052.translation: So cunning Nana nana nana voya voya nana nana nana Nobody knew if he was fish or fowl Voya voya voya nana nana nana So cunning voya voya nana He grazed his big bell reindeer down below,  Voya voya nana nana A hideout for boys when in need When they are discovered stealing Voya voya nana nana.
3052.original_formatted: Stuora gávvila , nana nana nana voja voja nana nana nana , ii oktage diehtán , leago guolli dahe loddi , voja voja voja nana nana nana , stuora gávvila , voja voja nana , mieđábealde stuora bielluin guđodii , voja voja nana nana , bárdnelunttaid dorvu , go heahti bođii , go gávnnahalle suolabarggus , voja voja nana nana .
3052.translation_formatted: So cunning Nana nana nana voya voya nana nana nana Nobody knew if he was fish or fowl Voya voya voya nana nana nana So cunning voya voya nana He grazed his big bell reindeer down below ,  Voya voya nana nana A hideout for boys when in need When they are discovered stealing Voya voya nana nana .

3053.original: Ja bártnit háliide juohkehaš dan bártni iežaset mielde dan_dihte go son leai nu gávvil.
3053.translation: And the guys all wanted that guy along because he was so cunning.
3053.original_formatted: Ja bártnit háliide juohkehaš dan bártni iežaset mielde dan_dihte go son leai nu gávvil .
3053.translation_formatted: And the guys all wanted that guy along because he was so cunning .

3054.original: Ja dakka dan áigge veaháš riidale sámit gaskaneaset, ja suoláde nuppit nuppiin, ja nuppit sokče nuppiid, go nuppit ledje suoládeame.
3054.translation: And at that time the Sámi were striving against each other somewhat,  and stealing from each other,  and spying on each other when they were stealing.
3054.original_formatted: Ja dakka dan áigge veaháš riidale sámit gaskaneaset , ja suoláde nuppit nuppiin , ja nuppit sokče nuppiid , go nuppit ledje suoládeame .
3054.translation_formatted: And at that time the Sámi were striving against each other somewhat ,  and stealing from each other ,  and spying on each other when they were stealing .

3055.translation: And in this way they often got caught in the act of stealing.
3055.translation_formatted: And in this way they often got caught in the act of stealing .

3214.original: Loahppa lehkos Ipmila askkis, dego mánná lea eatni askkis, gos lea sus buoremus dorvu.
3214.translation: May they come in the end into God's embrace,  like a child in its mother's arms,  wherein lies its greatest protection.
